plan.title: Paired 3-group DE: treated A/B vs control, blood RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve blood samples from four human subjects, each measured under control, treated_a, and treated_b (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 13 columns; metadata.csv with subject and condition). The question has two parts: which genes respond to either treatment within a subject, and whether the two treatments differ from each other. Because each subject contributes one sample to every condition, the subject is a blocking term placed before the condition in the design; the paired DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test with full design ~ subject + condition against reduced ~ subject finds every gene that differs between any of the three conditions within subjects, and pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a) resolve which treatment drives each response and separate the two treatments from each other. The profile records raw gene-level counts from Salmon with no statement of the length correction and no quantification files, so per rule R-0169 the model fits the counts as delivered with no length offset and the report states that a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression. Analysis order: sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA, sample distances) before any test; minimal pre-filter; the LRT plus named contrasts; ashr shrinkage of the reported fold changes (the treated_b vs treated_a contrast is not a single model coefficient, so ashr, not apeglm, per R-0040); BH adjustment within each contrast; per-contrast fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark and the staged WikiPathways human collection; a report with fit diagnostics, both fold-change estimates, p-value histograms, leading edges, and a full reproducibility record. No KEGG collection is served.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
